title: SREV-002 legacy password SHA1 hex shape

official_hash_api_shape.description: CryptCreateHash, CryptHashData, CryptGetHashParam(HP_HASHVAL) produce binary digest bytes; CryptoAPI is deprecated in favor of CNG

legacy_format.description: Legacy password is 40 hex WCHARs from SHA1 over at most 64 WCHARs of password

current_format.description: Current password is 64 base64 WCHARs encoding [16 byte salt][32 byte SHA256 hash]

legacy_bug_shape.description: Historical encoder shifted the high nibble by 8 instead of 4; high hex digit always encoded as 0

compatibility_boundary.description: HashPassword(..., LegacyBug=true) preserves old shape; legacy verification accepts both historical buggy and canonical SHA1 hex; new writes remain SHA256/salt only

runtime_matrix.description: Windows runtime gate covering known legacy-bug hash, canonical SHA1 hash, and current SHA256/salt password configs all authenticating as expected

contracts: CryptCreateHash creates a hash object and returns a handle
CryptHashData appends bytes to the hash object
CryptGetHashParam(HP_HASHVAL) returns binary digest bytes; hex encoding is application-owned
Legacy SHA1 hex encoding bug must be represented as an explicit LegacyBug switch, not a silent shift
40-character legacy verification first checks the historical buggy shape, then canonical SHA1 hex
SHA256/salt password writes remain the only set-password output path
Automatic legacy-to-current rewrite requires a separate runtime gate because authorization must not mutate config as a side effect
